correctness.rationale: The subgroup classification follows from the prime quotient G/P and the unique chain of subgroups in the cyclic kernel. At level i there are exactly p^(a-i) q-containing subgroups. Two q-containing subgroups that are not comparable have intersection equal to the smaller kernel subgroup; if they permuted, their product would have order p^m q^2, impossible for a subgroup of G. Thus comparability is equivalent to permutability. This yields the exact partner count 2a-j+1+S_j and the stated normalized sum. The packaged replay directly checks all subgroup products and relative degrees in four semidirect products.

originality.rationale: The 2018 primary source develops the same relative invariant and explicitly computes prime-kernel semidirect families C_p semidirect C_{q^n}. Its full-text family classification does not include the cyclic prime-power kernel C_{p^a} semidirect C_q with a>=2. The later relative cyclic paper restricts to cyclic subgroups and therefore does not imply the all-subgroup formula. Targeted published-result searches found no exact formula or comparable-subgroup criterion for this family.

value.rationale: The relative subgroup commutativity function is an established invariant with explicit semidirect-product calculations forming a central part of the 2018 primary paper. The final theorem gives the complete function for a natural infinite metacyclic Frobenius family with a qualitatively richer subgroup lattice: nonnormal Frobenius subgroups occur at every p-level. The comparability criterion is structural, and the formula covers every subgroup rather than a single global probability.
